name: Observation of Reactor Electron Antineutrino Disappearance in the RENO Experiment
title: Observation of Reactor Electron Antineutrino Disappearance in the RENO Experiment

claim.quote: Observation of Reactor Electron Antineutrino Disappearance in the RENO Experiment

summary.plain: RENO's two identical detectors, near and far from an array of six reactors in Korea, observed the disappearance of reactor electron antineutrinos, consistent with neutrino oscillations, with a significance of 4.9 standard deviations. From the deficit it determined the θ13 mixing angle: sin²2θ13 = 0.113 ± 0.013 ± 0.019.
summary.technical: In a 229-day data-taking period (11 Aug 2011 - 26 Mar 2012) the far (near) detector observed 17102 (154088) electron-antineutrino candidates; the ratio of observed to expected antineutrinos in the far detector is 0.920±0.009(stat)±0.014(syst), giving sin²(2θ₁₃) = 0.113±0.013(stat)±0.019(syst) from a rate-only analysis; disappearance observed with a significance of 4.9 standard deviations.

why_it_matters.value: The abstract reports the observed disappearance of reactor electron antineutrinos, consistent with neutrino oscillations, and determines sin²2θ13 from a rate-only analysis; the antineutrinos come from six 2.8 GWth reactors at the Yonggwang Nuclear Power Plant and are detected at 294 m and 1383 m from the reactor array centre.
why_it_matters.quote: Antineutrinos from six 2.8 GW$_{th}$ reactors at the Yonggwang Nuclear Power Plant in Korea, are detected by two identical detectors located at 294 m and 1383 m, respectively, from the reactor array center.

significance.quote: with a significance of 4.9 standard deviations
